summary: This is a Docusaurus plugin that generates RSS 2.0 feeds from blog posts. It creates a main site-wide feed containing the latest articles, plus optional per-tag and per-series feeds so readers can subscribe to specific topics. The plugin extracts clean article content from the built HTML, respects author and tag metadata, converts all URLs to absolute ones, and optionally includes featured images.

explanations.70: This utility joins URL path segments using forward slashes (POSIX style) and ensures the result starts with a slash, so paths combine correctly regardless of how they're passed in.
explanations.82: This constructs a complete absolute URL by combining the site's domain (siteUrl), the base path where the site lives (baseUrl), and a relative path—like building https://example.com/blog/my-post.
explanations.94: This examines a file extension and returns the matching MIME type string that goes into RSS enclosure tags to tell readers what kind of file the image is.
explanations.119: This strips out invisible or control characters (like zero-width spaces or old control codes) that can break XML parsers, then trims whitespace.
explanations.143: This merges three selector lists—critical ones that must always be removed (headers, SVGs), default ones for common UI artifacts, and any custom ones the user provided—into one final list.
explanations.149: This reads the built HTML file for a blog post, uses a DOM parser to find and clean the article content by removing unwanted elements, then returns sanitized HTML safe for RSS.
explanations.162: Cheerio's `.first()` grabs the first matching element; if nothing matches (`.length` is 0), the condition fails and we try the next selector as a fallback.
explanations.178: This loops through Docusaurus code snippet wrappers and replaces them with just the bare code block, so RSS readers get cleaner code blocks without extra styling containers.
explanations.195: This computes a URL-friendly slug for a post: either from explicit front matter, or derived from the filename (handling special cases like folder/index.md files), then lowercased with underscores converted to hyphens.
explanations.263: Instead of using the current time, the feed's 'last updated' date is set to the newest post's date—this prevents unchanged feeds from being rewritten and re-uploaded on every build.
explanations.272: This array will hold XML strings like `<dc:creator>Author Name</dc:creator>` for each post; it's built in parallel with the items and injected into the final RSS via a separate XML manipulation step.
explanations.276: This converts the authors field (which might be a string, an array, or missing) into a consistent array format so the next step can map over it safely.
explanations.304: This builds an absolute URL for a post's featured image by combining the site URL, base path, and image path from front matter—needed so RSS readers can actually fetch the image.
explanations.309: The description starts as cleaned plain text, then if images are enabled, prepends an HTML `` tag so the image appears inline in readers that support HTML descriptions.
explanations.333: This spread operator conditionally adds an `enclosure` object (which tells RSS readers where to download an attached file and its type) only if we have both an image URL and a valid MIME type.
explanations.345: The 'feed' library's `.rss2()` method generates a complete RSS 2.0 XML document as a string; this is then post-processed with Cheerio to add features the library doesn't natively support.
explanations.352: Cheerio is told to parse in 'xmlMode' so it handles the XML syntax correctly and doesn't add HTML-specific transformations that would break the RSS structure.
explanations.368: This loop adds each post's author tags (stored earlier in `creatorMarkup`) into the corresponding XML `<item>` element by position—safe because both arrays maintain the same order.
explanations.409: This dynamically imports the 'feed' package (rather than requiring it at the top) because it's an ESM module; older Node versions need this async approach.
explanations.447: Glob finds all `.md` and `.mdx` files in the blog directory, excluding paths matching ignore patterns like archived posts.
explanations.467: If a post has no explicit date in front matter, the file's creation timestamp (birthtime) is used instead as a fallback.
explanations.505: The filter removes any posts marked as `published: false` in front matter and any posts where the HTML extraction failed (no body content).
explanations.512: This takes only the first `maxItems` posts from the sorted list, with a minimum of 1 to ensure at least something is always in the feed.
explanations.563: `.values()` gets just the groups (the values from the Map) since we don't need the group labels as keys for iteration.
explanations.572: Posts are skipped from their tag feed if fewer than `minPostsPerTagFeed` posts share that tag—this prevents feeds with only one item.
explanations.611: Similar to the site-wide feed, topic feeds are capped at `topicMaxItems` per-topic instead of the global `maxItems` to keep per-topic feeds smaller and faster.
